citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
It has been greater than 6 months since the last semi annual review of the facilities, according to documentation available
during inspection. The last documented review was recorded in the May 2025 IACUC meeting minutes, although a facility
representative verbally stated they have been conducted since then. Not conducting an inspection of the animal facilities
on a semi annual basis does not allow the IACUC to determine if the facility has been maintained in a manner to protect
the welfare of the animals. It is the responsibility of the IACUC to conduct semi annual inspections of the research facility's
animal areas to ensure they are maintained in a manner that protects the health and safety of the animals.
To be corrected by 31 October 2026.

citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
The facility is not preparing reports of their semi annual review of the facilities. Failure to prepare and submit reports to the
Institutional Official (IO) does not allow for proper internal communication regarding status of the animal care and use
program. Every six months, upon completion of the program review and facility inspection, the IACUC must provide
reports of its evaluations to the IO to ensure that they are aware of the current status of the animal program, facilities, and
procedures. After completing the program review and the inspection of the animal facilities, the IACUC must prepare
reports of their evaluations that a majority of members must sign, and submit the reports to the Institutional Official.
To be corrected by next semi annual review.

*****An adult male cat "Cashew" was acquired as a stray according to acquisition documentation. The cat has a tipped left
ear typical of feral cats that were altered as part of trap-neuter-release programs.
*****Five adult dogs "Bella", "Dexter", "Nyla", "Molly" & "Akira" and one adult cat "Ben" were acquired as owner release
but no certification paperwork was signed.
These animals from non-USDA-licensed sources were acquired without a certificate stating that the animals were “born
and raised” on the person’s premise and that “fewer than 25 dogs and/or cats” were sold that year. Without this
certification, there is no definite guarantee of the animals’ origins and therefore the adequacy of utilizing these animals for
teaching cannot be determined. If dogs or cats are acquired from any person not licensed or registered under the Act and
not a pound or shelter, the research facility must obtain a certification that the animals were born and raised on the
person’s premises and that the person has sold fewer than 25 dogs and/or cats that year.
To be corrected from this date forward.

*****The registrant does not have proper identification for 2 live cats ("Ben" & "Cashew") and 7 live dogs ("Bella",
"Churro", "JC Penney", "Kiera", "Poppy", "Radar" & "Rocky") that were acquired. These 9 animals do not have a tag,
tattoo or collar with individual numbers according to records provided during inspection. A facility representative stated
that all dogs do have a microchip.
*****The registrant does not have a microchip reader available to scan the dogs with microchips at the holding facility.
Failure to properly identify live dogs and cats in research may result in errors and does not allow APHIS Officials to carry
out their duties. All live dogs or cats acquired by a research facility shall be identified at the time of acquisition in one of
the following ways listed in this subpart.
To be corrected by 03 September 2026.

At the time of the inspection, the facility had not completed and documented an annual review of the contingency plan.
The plan was last documented, reviewed, and approved in August of 2024. Timely review of the contingency plan ensure
that any needed changes are made, and communicated to all personnel that have a role or responsibilities in the plan, to
help avoid animal discomfort, illness, injury, or death in the event of an emergency or disaster or unforeseen animal
incident. The registrant must ensure that the contingency plan is reviewed on at least an annual basis to confirm that it
adequately addresses the criteria listed in Section 2.38(l)(1) and must also maintain documentation of those reviews, to
include any amendments or changes made to the plan since the previous year's review.
To be corrected by 14 September 2026.

Unopened bags of dog and cat food and an open bag of cat litter are being stored directly on the floor in storage areas at
the research site. Improper storage of food and bedding supplies may lead to spoilage and contamination. All supplies of
food and bedding must be stored off the floor and away from walls, to allow cleaning underneath and around the supplies.
Open supplies of food and bedding must be kept in leakproof containers with tightly fitting lids to prevent contamination
and spoilage.
To be corrected by 19 August 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the Attending Veterinarian.
